solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Siberian river with length and shape

parts.note: the Ob flows north across Siberia to the Arctic

explanation.surface: A geography note describing a Siberian river's length and outline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ob is a crossword staple among rivers. The surface asks you to picture a river's course, but the last word, 'shape', is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain category-and-member pairing: the oblong, a rectangle longer than it is wide, is one named shape.

clue.text: Skater out in West Indies to practise another sport?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the West Indies abbreviation
out means the skater's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An ice skater in the Caribbean takes up a different pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterskiing is a sport, a different one from skating, done on skis towed by a boat.

clue.text: Husband joining unruly originals blended language

indicators.note: joining means the husband letter attaches itself to the end of the rearranged word
unruly means the letters behave badly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband joins a group of unruly founders, speaking a hybrid tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Irish is the form of English spoken in Ireland, a mix of English and Irish features.

clue.text: Watch pressure slowly escape

explanation.surface: An instruction to monitor a gauge as pressure bleeds away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a noun (a timepiece) but works as the verb see.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: liquid that oozes out through a crack little by little is getting away gradually.

clue.text: Initial written cryptically around chimney enlightened people

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the chimney word
written cryptically means the letters are set down in a scrambled form

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for a chimney

explanation.surface: An initial carved in code around a chimney by people in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: The chimney word is Scots, the dialect where a lum is a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illuminati were a secret society claiming special enlightenment; the Latin word means enlightened ones.

clue.text: Distinguished singer keen to make comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the word travels back the way it came, right to left

explanation.surface: A celebrated singer eager to return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the familiar story of a retired star's comeback, which is exactly what the letters of AVID do.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word diva means goddess, and it came to name a celebrated leading lady of opera.

clue.text: Horned beast the thing with one foot raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters lifts the last to the top, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: an animal's foot is a paw

explanation.surface: A horned animal standing with one hoof lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture of a beast with a paw raised fits the wordplay neatly: in the grid the whole string ITIPAW is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description: the wapiti is a large North American deer, and its antlers are called horns in everyday speech.

clue.text: Company receives order beginning to march with soldier

indicators.note: the beginning of march is its first letter

explanation.surface: A military company gets its marching orders and is joined by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command to march, but it is OM, the Order of Merit. 'With' is also wordplay (AND), not a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A general-to-specific definition: a commando is one kind of soldier, trained for raids behind enemy lines.

clue.text: Female supporter incarcerated shows little intellectual capacity

explanation.surface: A woman who backed a cause is locked up and shows she is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female supporter' suggests a woman who backs someone; it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: saying someone has only one brain cell is a joking jibe that they are not bright.

clue.text: Maybe comma adds nothing to one publication

explanation.surface: An editor's gripe that a comma contributes nothing to a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma here is not punctuation but a butterfly, named for the comma-shaped mark on its wing; 'maybe' signals that it is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the adult winged stage of an insect is its imago, and a comma butterfly is one such adult.

clue.text: Share common ground having finished circuit

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Runners who have completed a lap end up on the same stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the wordplay pieces arrive in the order the answer reads them.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative phrase for the verb: two areas that partly cover each other have ground in common.

clue.text: Posh princess uses mains leads for element

parts.note: a rani is an Indian princess

indicators.note: whatever leads comes at the front, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: first letters of uses and mains

explanation.surface: A posh princess plugs into the mains to power a heating element.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about electrical mains leads and a heating element; 'leads' actually means first letters, and 'element' is a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A category-and-member pairing: uranium, the radioactive metal, is one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Theatre Cat in squall losing tail

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, and here it is lost

parts.note: GUST, a squall, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A theatre cat caught in a gust of wind and losing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Gus the Theatre Cat is from T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, the source of the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A named character: Eliot's poem Gus: The Theatre Cat gives him that very title.

clue.text: See 21
Outline location accommodating upper-class in sprawling hotel

indicators.note: the location holds the other letters inside it, as a hotel accommodates guests
sprawling suggests the letters are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: A grand hotel spread over a site welcomes upper-class guests.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British usage from the 1950s U and non-U debate about upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is the dark shape or outline of a figure seen against light.

clue.text: Certain changes in Danube and Nile

indicators.note: changes made in the rivers' names alter the order of their letters

explanation.surface: A remark that there are certain changes happening along two great rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' looks like it means 'some' changes; it is the definition, meaning sure.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: what cannot be denied is beyond doubt, the sense of certain here.

clue.text: Do cut off a sexual urge, providing excuse

indicators.note: something cut off is severed from the end, so DO is chopped from the tail

explanation.surface: Someone claims that curbing their desires gives them a handy excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb, but it is the letters DO, cut from the end of A LIBIDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an alibi began as a claim to have been elsewhere and widened to any excuse.

clue.text: Fool with heraldic device not quite put together

indicators.note: not quite means the heraldic word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an emblem is a heraldic device

explanation.surface: A jester with a coat of arms that is not quite finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to fit parts together, or to gather people into a group.

clue.text: Land that's green and somewhat pleasant

indicators.note: 'somewhat' means to some extent, so only a part of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An echo of Blake's 'England's green and pleasant land'.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue borrows the line 'England's green and pleasant land' from Blake's hymn Jerusalem, so the definition hides in a quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a meadow, grassland that is green by nature.

clue.text: Two passes for Maradona?

parts.note: a pass in a game is a go, a turn

explanation.surface: A football question about a pair of passes played to Maradona.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all football, but neither pass is kicked: one is to pass away, the other is a turn. Diego Maradona was the Argentine football star.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Maradona is one famous Diego, the question mark showing he stands for the first name.

clue.text: Somehow at peace crossing southern region in NZ

indicators.note: crossing means the jumbled letters go across, and so round, the next letter
somehow means the letters are put together in some unstated way

explanation.surface: A southern part of New Zealand, somehow at peace.
explanation.walkthrough: AT PEACE rearranged as EATCAPE takes S after EA.
explanation.definitionFit: East Cape is the easternmost point of New Zealand's North Island and the region around it.

clue.text: Forger in situ, no saint, into working for museums group

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A forger, no saint, is caught at work in the museums.
explanation.walkthrough: Forger looks like a counterfeiter; it is a blacksmith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Smithsonian Institution in Washington runs a group of national museums and research centres.

clue.text: I want to cuddle daughter? Absolutely

indicators.note: to cuddle someone is to wrap your arms round them

explanation.surface: A parent asks whether they want a hug from their daughter, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a question and its reply; the reply is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection synonym: both are emphatic ways of saying yes.

clue.text: Everything or unspecified amount for an audience?

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A promoter wonders whether to seat the whole crowd or just some of it at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves pull against each other, everything against some, yet they share a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: the sum is the total, the whole amount taken together.

clue.text: Old woman on edge about year in chaotic state

indicators.note: about means the old woman and edge words together go round the next letter
in a down clue on means placed above, so the old woman comes before the edge

parts.note: ma is mother, an old woman
a hem is an edge of cloth

explanation.surface: An old woman on edge for about a year, in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos.

clue.text: Give drugs to banish cold and help settle

indicators.note: to banish is to send into exile

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice: dose to cure a cold and help the patient rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a medical cure for a cold; the definition is about disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: a go-between who mediates helps the two sides reach agreement.

clue.text: Continuous pain? One should ring hospital

indicators.note: a ring encircles, so the one goes round the hospital

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone in constant pain is urged to phone the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like phoning; it means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an ache is a dull pain that goes on, as against a sharp stab.

clue.text: Complete disorder with an unknown spanner thrown in?

indicators.note: something thrown in lands inside, as a spanner is thrown in the works

explanation.surface: Throwing a spanner in the works leads to complete chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The spanner is not the tool thrown into the works but an arch, which spans.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: from Greek 'without a ruler', anarchy is lawless disorder.

clue.text: Giving away copyright lightens up relief

indicators.note: whatever you give away you no longer have

parts.note: C = copyright, as in the © symbol; removed

explanation.surface: Giving up copyright eases the mind and brings relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving away' fits the charity of the answer but here means removing C from CALMS.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of relief: help for the poor, which is what alms are.

clue.text: Slippery character back needing check calls for doctor

indicators.note: sending a word back returns it the way it came

explanation.surface: A slippery type with a bad back who needs a check-up calls the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Leech is an old word for a doctor, from when physicians bled patients with leeches.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense: leech was the Old English word for a physician.

clue.text: Ample set rebuilt to accommodate one photography option?

indicators.note: to accommodate means the rebuilt letters house the next piece
rebuilt means the letters are reconstructed in another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A spacious film set rebuilt to suit one way of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: AMPLE SET rearranged as TMELAPSE takes I after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse filming shoots frames at intervals so slow change appears fast, an option on many cameras.
